hypotheses.construction_plan: Instantiate Sym_T(a,b) at (a,b)=(i,j). The raw expression is then the identity image of that instantiated symmetric invariant object. The object is unchanged under simultaneous argument swap a <-> b.
required_assumptions: T is defined for swapped arguments
Addition is available for the two T terms
hypotheses.rationale: The two terms of the raw expression form the S2-symmetric completion of a bivariate function T. This captures why the expression is structurally invariant under swapping i and j.

hypotheses.construction_plan: Instantiate the single bivariate kernel K(a,b)=T(a,b) at (a,b)=(i,j). The identity operator gives T(i,j). Applying the argument permutation operator to the same instantiation gives T(j,i). Thus both T terms are orbit images of one kernel under S2.
required_assumptions: T is a symmetric-callable bivariate function symbol
hypotheses.rationale: The two indexed calls are evaluations of the same function T with argument order exchanged. They are generated from one repeated kernel by the identity and index-permutation operators.
